market_pulse.note: Slid 0.85%, snapping its recent record-setting win streak.
Fell 0.18% as Treasury yields rose and earnings reactions were punishing for some AI names.
Down 0.06%, roughly flat after a volatile session for chip-adjacent stocks.
Rose about 1%, even as hopes for a Strait of Hormuz deal continued.

themes.title: Storage-chip earnings punished hard
themes.summary: Sandisk and Western Digital both tumbled sharply after earnings, weighing on the broader semiconductor group despite strong AI-driven demand narratives.

themes.title: July layoffs hit a two-year low
themes.summary: Employers announced 33,429 job cuts in July, down 27% from June — but AI was cited as the top reason for a fifth straight month.

themes.title: Strait of Hormuz deal still in focus
themes.summary: Iran's parliament is reportedly reviewing a bill affecting vessel transit as talks continue; markets stayed cautious on the unfinished deal.

themes.title: Earnings season delivers a mixed bag
themes.summary: Motorola Solutions and Albemarle jumped on strong results while Honeywell Aerospace tumbled over 21% on a weak 2026 outlook.

themes.title: AI capex debate still weighing on tech
themes.summary: Investors remain hyper-focused on whether heavy AI infrastructure spending is translating into profit, a theme carried through this week's AMD, SpaceX, Sandisk and Western Digital reactions.

sectors.name: Energy
sectors.note: Among the pockets holding up the market amid the broader pullback.

sectors.name: Semiconductors
sectors.note: Also cushioning losses, though the AI-spending debate continues.

sectors.name: Industrials
sectors.note: Split sharply — Parker-Hannifin up 7.6% on earnings, Honeywell Aerospace down over 21%.

sectors.name: Rate-sensitive sectors
sectors.note: Under pressure as Treasury yields climb ahead of Friday's jobs report.

watch_list.why: Economists expect payrolls up roughly 80,000 and unemployment holding at 4.2% — a notable miss or beat could quickly move rate-cut expectations.
A 21%+ single-day drop on lowered 2026 sales guidance is a large move — worth understanding whether it's company-specific or a read on broader industrial demand.
AI has now been the top-cited layoff reason for five straight months, concentrated in tech — worth tracking whether that broadens to other sectors.
